testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system is very low on pressure, what happens?

options.text: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
Lights on the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one air system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. You must stop the vehicle safely and have the air system repaired.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what is the result?

options.text: Brakes do not work as well as they would without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Jackknifing risk decreases.
questions.explanation: When only the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, jackknifing risk is reduced. The driver keeps better steering control. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing to one side.

questions.question: How long should air pressure take to build up in a single air system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three minutes
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with a single air brake system, pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within three minutes after the engine reaches operating speed.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on hazard lights and continue driving.
Safely pull off the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and stop.
questions.explanation: If the air pressure warning light or buzzer comes on, stop and park the vehicle right away. This warning means there is a problem in the air brake system that needs repair.

questions.question: When should you not use the parking brake?

options.text: When your vehicle is stopped on level ground.
When your vehicle is stopped on a slight slope.
When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
When your vehicle's other brakes seem to be working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if the brakes are very hot from steep downhill driving or if they are wet in freezing weather. Hot brakes can be damaged by the parking brake. Wet brakes in freezing temperatures may ice up and lock the vehicle.

questions.question: What must be installed on an air tank in an air-braked vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: A check valve
questions.explanation: All air tanks on air-braked vehicles must have one-way check valves. These are placed between the air compressor and the first reservoir. They stop air from leaking out if there is a leak.

questions.question: What type of air brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brake systems
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These systems have two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning light. This light is usually red and may also have a buzzer.

questions.question: What is true about an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: It cannot be used with air brakes.
It should only be used on dry pavement.
It helps you keep control when braking.
It only works if all axles have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you keep control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS works with air braking systems. It helps keep the vehicle under control and stops wheels from locking up during hard braking on slippery surfaces. ABS provides benefits even if it is on only one axle.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Stop the vehicle from speeding up on hills
Stop the vehicle from speeding up going downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent wheel lockup
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops the vehicle's wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, what should you do?

options.text: Use one foot on the gas and one foot on the brake.
Safely pull off the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop your vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, how do you apply the parking brake?

options.text: Pull out a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
Pull out a round red knob.
Pull out a square green knob.
Pull out a black round knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks with manual drains at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what air pressure should build up in the system?
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before driving, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: When should you NOT use the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot.
When the brakes are very cold.
When there is snow on the ground.
When there is water on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake when brakes are very hot from long use on steep hills. Hot brakes can be damaged. Also avoid the parking brake if brakes are wet and it is freezing, as they may ice up and lock the vehicle.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, what is true?

options.text: You can only brake if enough air remains in the tanks.
You can apply the brakes 14 times before the air runs out.
You can drive normally and check the brakes later.
You must stay 100 feet away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only brake if enough air remains in the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. There may be a leak. You can still brake only if enough air is left in the tanks.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with dual air brakes, what should a driver do?

options.text: Warm up the vehicle to make sure fuel reaches the engine.
Wait until the air compressor builds 100 psi in both systems before driving.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the pedal 20 times to build pressure, then drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the air compressor builds 100 psi in both systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: When does the safety valve on the first air tank open?
questions.correctAnswerText: When pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety valve on the first tank releases air if pressure gets too high, usually at 150 psi. If this valve opens, there is a problem with the system that needs repair.

questions.question: What is true about air brakes?

options.text: They work well for stopping large vehicles.
They are not allowed on large vehicles.
They only work well in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work well for stopping large vehicles.
questions.explanation: When properly maintained, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with dual air brake systems?

options.text: They keep air pressure in the brakes even when the engine is off.
They keep some air pressure in the brakes when the engine is off.
The engine must run to build air pressure for the brakes to work.
They keep air pressure for up to four hours after shutdown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine must run to build air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks at the end of each day. This removes oil and water that builds up inside the tanks.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle
To stop the vehicle during normal driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake whenever you park your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when going down a steep hill?

options.text: Shift into a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking power
Downshift instead of using the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking power
questions.explanation: On a downgrade, use engine braking as your main way to control speed. Shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Use brakes only when you need extra slowing or stopping.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: To let rainwater into the tank
To remove water and compressor oil from the tank
They must stay open while driving

questions.correctAnswerText: To remove water and compressor oil from the tank
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks collect water and compressor oil. Drains remove these liquids. If you don't drain the tanks, damage can occur. Use manual drains at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: Which vehicles must have emergency brakes?

options.text: They are not required on trucks
They are only required on trailers

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required on tractors
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must work using mechanical force.
